purpose: Prioritize 10 local Hays source photo sets with high diagnostic potential after five image QA passes
scope: These are precise identification-proof requirements from authoritative source descriptions; they are not observed positive characters unless specifically described as visible.

provenance.regional_flora: User-uploaded Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, Poaceae section
provenance.modern: Flora of North America, Kew POWO/GrassBase where regional Flora uses older names or lacks species

records.name: Aegilops cylindrica
records.observed: Jointed, slender, cylindrical spike and detached spike sections visible in Hays photos.
records.exact: Spikelets tightly fitted in niches along unbranched 2-sided flattened axis; sessile spikelets usually 2–5-flowered; upper spikelet lemma/glume awns about 3–8 cm; ligule <1 mm.
records.source: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), user-provided Poaceae PDF
records.proof: An intact mature spike plus separated one-node/one-spikelet segment, with ruler, and a ligule/collar photo.
records.lookalikes: Hordeum spp., Triticum aestivum and other goatgrasses

records.name: Tridentopsis elongata
records.observed: Excellent grass habit, narrow panicle, several close spikelets and partial collar views.
records.exact: Regional Flora's older Tridens muticus var. elongatus concept: 2nd glume usually 6–8 mm long and 3–7-nerved; blades usually 3–4 mm wide, versus var. muticus's usually 1-nerved glume ~5 mm or less and blades 1–2 mm wide.
records.source: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), user-provided Poaceae PDF
records.proof: One flattened second glume with nervation illuminated, at least two individual spikelets and a 1-mm scale; measure blade width.

records.name: Echinochloa walteri
records.observed: Awned panicles, wetland setting and strongly hairy leaf sheaths have excellent supporting Hays views.
records.exact: Sheaths usually with papilla-based hirsute/hispid hairs; spikelets about 3–5 mm without awn; lower floret lemma awns commonly 1.5–6 cm, but occasionally shortened or absent.
records.source: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), user-provided Poaceae PDF
records.proof: Sheath-hair bases in sharp focus next to ruler, plus two mature spikelets measuring unawned body and lemma awn.
records.lookalikes: Echinochloa crus-galli, Echinochloa muricata, other barnyardgrasses

records.name: Sphenopholis obtusata
records.observed: Dense to elongate spike-like panicles and sheath/collar views from Hays.
records.exact: Second glume much broader/obovate and blunt-tipped; spikelets shiny and 2–3-flowered, about 1.5–5 mm long; membranous ligule 1.5–3 mm.
records.source: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), user-provided Poaceae PDF
records.proof: Isolated spikelet with broad upper glume face, plus whole floret count and true membranous ligule.

records.name: Coelorachis cylindrica
records.observed: Thin cylindrical jointed flowering axes very well shown in multiple Hays observations.
records.exact: Regional Flora Coelorachis cylindrica concept: inflorescence about 3 mm thick, axis jointed with niches where spikelets fit, paired sessile fertile spikelet (pitted glume) and sterile pedicelled spikelet, ligule 0.5–1 mm.
records.source: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), user-provided Poaceae PDF
records.proof: Close view of one node showing the spikelet in niche and glume pit, with 1-mm ruler, plus a section disarticulating at the joint.

records.name: Paspalum langei
records.observed: Several two-ranked racemes and broad leaves supported by multiple Hays images.
records.exact: Panicles with 2–5 branches usually 4–8 cm; spikelets around 2.2–2.6 mm; first glume present on some or all; second glume and sterile lemma pubescent; leaf blades 7–18 mm wide.
records.source: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), user-provided Poaceae PDF
records.proof: Detached mature spikelets showing both glume faces and hair details with a millimeter scale.
records.lookalikes: Paspalum pubiflorum, Paspalum distichum and other branched Paspalum

records.name: Tridens congestus
records.observed: Short, compact/pink-tinged panicles with clear field habit.
records.exact: Panicles 5–10 cm long; glumes and lemmas thin, papery and often pink-tinged; lemma apex deeply cleft.
records.source: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), user-provided Poaceae PDF
records.proof: Dissect mature lemma and photograph its deeply cleft apex, glumes and 1-mm ruler.
records.lookalikes: Tridens flavus, Tridens muticus and other tridens

records.name: Pappophorum bicolor
records.observed: Feathery seedheads against dry rocky Hays grassland, with close ripe florets in one observation.
records.exact: Typically pink panicles; fertile lemma body about 3–4 mm and apex bearing approximately 11–15 unequal awns; 2–3 bisexual florets plus sterile upper florets.
records.source: Flora of North America Pappophorum bicolor account (Reeder), crosschecked with Kew/GrassBase and Texas A&M
records.proof: Detach one mature lemma and count 11–15 unequal awns, show lemma body and 1-mm scale.
records.lookalikes: Other Pappophorum and feathery-awned grama grasses

records.name: Janochloa antidotalis
records.observed: One unusually complete eight-photo Hays series: panicle, spikelets, nodes, culm and collar.
records.exact: Rhizomatous perennial with swollen nodes and woody culms; panicles 10–45 cm, spikelets 2.4–3.4 mm; shorter lower glumes, usually 3–5-veined; lower floret staminate, upper fertile.
records.source: Flora of North America (under Panicum antidotale), and local 1999 Flora Panicum antidotale entry
records.proof: Clear rhizome/crown photo and detached mature spikelets with lower versus upper glumes and fertile floret under scale.
records.lookalikes: Panicum hallii, Panicum bergii and other blue panic look-alikes

records.name: Stapfochloa canterae
records.observed: Macro views of ciliate raceme axis, seedhead and scale-backed split spikelets, good local evidence.
records.exact: Differentiation from S. ciliata requires precise glume, fertile lemma, sterile floret and awn characters; gross fingerlike inflorescence alone is insufficient. Existing S. ciliata source key has 1 fertile and 2 small sterile florets and strongly ciliate fertile lemma.
records.source: Kew POWO/GrassBase Stapfochloa ciliata comparator; do not transfer ciliata dimensions onto canterae
records.proof: Compare matched spikelet dissections of verified canterae and ciliata at identical scales, with floret count and lemma hair distribution.
